refactoringLog.reason: GetRun/ListRuns release their lock before returning a *Run pointer to the caller; CompleteRun mutating that same pointer's fields afterward is a pre-existing data race. ListRuns hands out far more of these pointers per request than GetRun ever did, so it must close before this feature multiplies the exposure. CompleteRun now builds and stores a new *Run copy instead of mutating in place, making every returned *Run effectively immutable for its lifetime.

simpleDesign.note: No code was written or executed this session (see deviations) — cannot claim green tests for a change that was never applied.
ListRuns/RunsPage/encodeCursor/decodeCursor names describe exactly what each does, and reuse Run/RunStore/Status naming already established in model.go rather than inventing synonyms.

Paged-response shaping reuses the existing writeJSON/writeError convention in responses.go instead of a second one; the /runs HTML page reuses Root()'s hand-written-string pattern instead of introducing a templating engine.
No new files, no new package-level type beyond RunsPage, no new dependency — the ordering index is one new field plus one new method on the existing RunStore.

keyDecisions.decision: Ordering index is an atomically-swapped immutable []string (most-recent-first), prepended-to inside StartRun's existing mu.Lock() section
keyDecisions.reasoning: Lets ListRuns read the current order lock-free, so listing can never block or be blocked by StartRun/CompleteRun beyond their existing O(1) map-mutation critical section — required by the never-blocks NFR and the 200ms p95 / 10,000-run budget.

keyDecisions.decision: Pagination cursor is an opaque token wrapping the last-returned run ID, not a numeric offset
keyDecisions.reasoning: Runs are only ever prepended, so a numeric offset shifts under concurrent inserts and would skip or repeat entries across pages. An ID-anchored cursor is stable because prepends ahead of a given ID never move anything after it.

keyDecisions.decision: CompleteRun replaces the stored *Run with a new fully-populated copy instead of mutating the existing pointer's fields in place
keyDecisions.reasoning: Closes a pre-existing data race (GetRun/ListRuns hand out *Run pointers after releasing their lock) that ListRuns would otherwise multiply across every row of every page. See refactoringLog: Change Reference to Value.

keyDecisions.decision: Malformed cursor → 400; a cursor past the end or an unrecognized status → 200 with an empty page and no next cursor
keyDecisions.reasoning: The spec already mandates empty-page-not-error for past-the-end pagination; extending the same precedent to unrecognized status keeps both optional filters behaviorally consistent. A token that fails to decode at all is genuinely malformed input, not 'nothing found'.

keyDecisions.decision: Default page size 20; requested limit clamped (not rejected) to [1, 100]
keyDecisions.reasoning: The spec requires paging without specifying a number. A hard cap prevents a caller from requesting an effectively unbounded page, which would reintroduce the O(store size) response cost this feature exists to avoid.

keyDecisions.decision: Status filtering is a linear forward scan over the ordering-index snapshot with early stop once a page is filled; no secondary per-status index
keyDecisions.reasoning: At the NFR's 10,000-run scale, a bounded in-memory scan is sub-millisecond even in the worst case. A secondary per-status index today would be premature generalization — every write would update N buckets with no demonstrated need.

keyDecisions.decision: Duration is computed server-side from StartedAt/FinishedAt at response time, not stored on Run; in-progress runs render a static 'running' label with no live timer
keyDecisions.reasoning: Run already carries both timestamps, so a stored duration field would be pure duplication. A static label avoids introducing a client-side polling/auto-refresh mechanism the spec never asked for (YAGNI) — flagged in deviations since architecture-notes leaves this open pending product/UX sign-off.
